title: Annotator doodles and probes
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for weird examples, small probes, and micro-guidelines I want to keep handy when adjudicating or writing rules. Not a final playbook.

Quick context
- Running micro-adjudication sessions with 3 annotators — looking for recurring disagreements that should become explicit rules.
- Goal: lower annotator cognitive load by turning ~60% of frequent disputes into short, consistent heuristics.
- Sampling plan: random sample 500 conflict pairs across entity types, focus on ID/AMOUNT/DATE/ADDRESS, then stratify by tokenization anomalies (slashes, hashes, punctuation).

Notes-to-self / rough heuristics (work-in-progress)
1) Numeric IDs mixed with punctuation (invoice#123/2020, ref: INV-123_2020)
   - Label as ID if the token group is used as a reference/invoice/order across the doc.
   - If numeric chunk represents a human-readable date (e.g., 2020/12/01) mark as DATE instead.
   - If ambiguous and shows up in a list under a header like "Invoices" -> ID.

2) Ranges and spans ("3/1-3/5", "2020-01-02 to 2020-02-03")
   - Treat as DATE_RANGE when both ends parse as dates.
   - If left token is numeric without clear date context ("pages 12-14") label as QUANTITY/COUNT depending on header.
   - For now: prefer contextual header over pattern.

3) Currency with symbols and trailing words ("$5k", "£5,000.00", "USD 5000")
   - Normalize currency symbol -> ISO code in audit metadata, but label as AMOUNT.
   - Abbreviations like "5k" -> still AMOUNT, but flag low confidence if no separator.

4) Obfuscated PII (j***@example.com, j.smith(at)company)
   - If clearly an obfuscated email pattern -> PII-EMAIL.
   - If ambiguous (username-only like "john123") -> abstain unless adjacent token is domain-like.

5) Hyphenated names and titles ("Anne-Marie OConnor", "Smith-Jones, Jr.")
   - Include hyphens and trailing suffix as part of PERSON span.
   - Split only if punctuation clearly separates two distinct entities (comma + role).

6) URLs with query strings and tracking params
   - Label whole URL as URL. Do not try to split query param keys as separate entities.
   - If URL contains a token that is a product slug and we need PRODUCT labels, annotate separately only when UI shows product context.

7) Addresses: partial vs full
   - Street number + name + city -> ADDRESS_FULL.
   - Just city or landmark -> LOCATION.
   - PO boxes (PO Box 123) -> ADDRESS but mark structured=false in metadata.

Adjudication micro-protocol (for pairwise conflicts)
- Step 1: expose the local context (2 lines before/after), ask annotator whether the token is a referent or descriptor.
- Step 2: if still disagree, check header/section label in doc. If header exists, header wins.
- Step 3: if still tied, default to ABSTAIN; record small note with reason tag (tokenization|context|format).

Sample hard examples (from batch-17) and proposed decisions
- "Acme/Corp. invoice#123/2020 for 01-02-2020" -> ID: "invoice#123/2020"; ORG: "Acme/Corp."; DATE: "01-02-2020"
- "Ref: user_42" -> ID: "user_42" (if used as referent); otherwise abstain
- "Payment: USD5000 / completed" -> AMOUNT: "USD5000" (normalize to USD 5,000 in audit)
- "Visit 5/3 at 10am" -> ambiguous 5/3: could be date or ratio. If in calendar context -> DATE; else ask for header.

Tokenizer pitfalls I keep seeing
- Slashes: split on '/' yields spurious small tokens ("2020/12/01" -> [2020,12,01]) which breaks pattern matching. Prefer keeping slash-bound groups intact for initial label pass.
- CamelCase product names inside weird punctuation ("FooBar_v2.1") -> annotators tend to mark as PRODUCT but model tokenizers split badly. Add a hint: treat alphanum+punct sequences > 5 chars as single candidate.

Micro experiments to run (logging ideas)
- E1: show annotators same sample with tokenizer A (split-on-punct) vs tokenizer B (keep alphanum groups) and measure F1 on ID/URL/AMOUNT.
- E2: provide small "header-first" hint to half the annotators and see if adjudication disagreement drops.
- E3: let annotators tag low-confidence cases using a single-click "abstain-reason" menu (tokenization/context/format). Track which reason is most common.

Quick regex snippets I want to test (for pre-labeling / triage)
- invoice: (?i)\b(inv(oice)?[-_#]?\d{2,}|invoice#?\d+)\b
- simple currency: (?i)(?:\bUSD|\$|£|€)\s?\d{1,3}(?:[,.]\d{3})*(?:[.,]\d{2})?\b
- date-ish: \b\d{4}[/-]\d{1,2}[/-]\d{1,2}\b|\b\d{1,2}[/-]\d{1,2}[/-]\d{2,4}\b

To-do (short)
- Draft short "annotator cheat card" (1/2 page) that lists the 6 heuristics above.
- Run E1 (tokenizer A/B) on 500 samples; log percent where pre-tokenization changed label.
- Push small change to labeling UI to capture abstain_reason (see linked PR).

Open questions / friction points
- How often should we normalize currency in audit vs leave raw? downstream teams want ISO code for billing, but compliance wants raw evidence. Maybe store both.
- For hyphenated surnames, cultural variation: do we need locale-aware rules? Not enough data yet.
- Are adjudicators bonused for speed? Need to avoid incentives that push toward over-labeling.

Random doodles (brain dump)
- Could we use a lightweight inference step that suggests a label + confidence and annotator only confirms? Active learning with human in loop — but keep it optional.
- Small UX idea: show the full sentence with colored token suggestions (low saturation) instead of checkboxes; might reduce errors for small spans.

If you read this later: grep the batch exports for "/" conflicts and sort by freq (I expect invoice-like tokens and dates to top the list).

-- Priya
Last quick note: keep this file as a mutable scratchpad; when something becomes a stable rule, move it to confluence and link it in linked_artifacts.
